discord.intro: Bind a Discord bot to chat with your agent in servers and DMs. You'll need a Bot Token from the Discord Developer Portal.
discord.setupQuestion: How do I get a Bot Token?
discord.step1: Open the <2><0></0></2>, click <4>New Application</4>, then open the <6>Bot</6> tab.
discord.step2: <0>REQUIRED:</0> on the Bot page, under <3>Privileged Gateway Intents</3>, turn ON <5>Message Content Intent</5>. Without it the bot receives messages with an empty body and can't read what people say.
discord.step3: Click <1>Reset Token</1> → <3>Copy</3>. Paste it below. Keep it secret.
discord.step4: Open <1>OAuth2 → URL Generator</1>, tick scope <3>bot</3> and permissions <5>View Channels</5>, <7>Send Messages</7>, <9>Read Message History</9>; open the generated URL and invite the bot to your server.
discord.step5: Optional: paste <1>your</1> numeric Discord user ID below so the agent recognises owner-vs-stranger. Enable Discord → Settings → Advanced → <3>Developer Mode</3>, then right-click your name → <5>Copy User ID</5>.
discord.troubleBlank: <0>Bot sees blank messages?</0> Message Content Intent is off — re-enable it on the Bot page.
discord.troubleNoReply: <0>No replies in a server?</0> @-mention the bot; it stays silent in channels until addressed.
discord.ownerIdPlaceholder: Your Discord user ID (optional, enables owner trust signal)
discord.noOwner: ⚠ No owner registered — agent has no trust signal for Discord senders. Re-bind with your numeric user ID to enable.

telegram.errTokenFormat: Bot token format looks wrong. Expected <digits>:<base64> (e.g. 7981632450:AAH-...).
telegram.unbindConfirmMessage: The agent will stop receiving Telegram messages and lose all Telegram tools until you bind again.
telegram.intro: Bind a Telegram bot to chat with your agent in DMs and groups. You'll need a Bot Token from @BotFather.
telegram.setupQuestion: How do I get a Bot Token?
telegram.step1: Open Telegram, search <2><0></0></2>, start a chat. Send <4>/newbot</4>; pick a display name + username (must end in <6>bot</6>).
telegram.step2: BotFather replies with a token like <1>7981632450:AAH-kxRP...</1>. Paste it below.
telegram.step3: <0>Privacy mode — KEEP DEFAULT ON</0>. By default the bot only sees <2>/commands</2> and @-mentions in groups; this is the right behavior for almost all use cases (saves tokens, prevents spam). DMs are unaffected. Do NOT run <4>/setprivacy → Disable</4> unless you specifically want the bot to see every group message (rare research / note-taking bots only).
telegram.step4: Optional: send <1>/setjoingroups</1> → bot → <3>Enable</3> if you want the bot to be addable to groups.
telegram.step5: Optional: paste <1>your</1> Telegram @username below so the agent recognises owner-vs-stranger DMs. <3>After binding, send any message to the bot from your @username</3> — Telegram's API only reveals your numeric user_id on a real DM, so the trust signal activates on first contact (not at bind time).
telegram.troubleNoReply: <0>Group not getting replies?</0> @-mention the bot. Privacy mode is intentionally on — flipping it would make the bot try to reply to everything in the group.
telegram.usernamePlaceholder: Your Telegram @username (optional, enables owner trust signal)
telegram.ownerPending: ⏳ Owner registration pending — DM @{{bot}} on Telegram from @{{username}} once to activate the trust signal.
telegram.ownerPendingNote: (Telegram's API doesn't let bots resolve @usernames at bind time — we wait for the first matching DM, then auto-link.)
telegram.noOwner: ⚠ No owner registered — agent has no trust signal for Telegram DMs. Re-bind with your @username to enable.

slack.intro: Bind a Slack bot to enable messaging in DMs and channels. You'll need a Bot Token (<1>xoxb-...</1>) and an App-Level Token (<3>xapp-...</3>).
slack.setupQuestion: How do I get these tokens?
slack.step1: Open <2><0></0></2>, click <4>Create New App</4> → <6>From an app manifest</6>, pick your workspace.
slack.step2: Paste the YAML below into the manifest editor. You can edit <2>display_information.name</2> (the app name in your workspace admin) and <5>features.bot_user.display_name</5> (the bot's name in DMs and @-mentions) — the defaults are placeholders. Leave the scopes / events / <7>socket_mode_enabled</7> bits as-is. Then click <10>Next</10> → <13>Create</13>. Slack will pre-configure ~16 OAuth scopes, 5 event subscriptions, Socket Mode, and the bot user.
slack.step3: On the app page, click <1>Install App</1> → <4>Install to Workspace</4> → <6>Allow</6>. Copy the <8>Bot User OAuth Token</8> (<10>xoxb-...</10>) into the field below.
slack.step4: Click <1>Basic Information</1> → scroll to <4>App-Level Tokens</4> → <6>Generate Token and Scopes</6>. Add the <8>connections:write</8> scope, click Generate, and copy the token (<10>xapp-...</10>) into the second field below.
slack.step5: After binding, invite the bot to any channel where it should listen: <1>/invite @NarraNexus</1>. DMs work automatically.

homeAssistant.title: Smart Home (Home Assistant)
homeAssistant.intro: Connect this agent to your Home Assistant to let it query and control your smart-home devices. Enter your HA URL and a Long-Lived Access Token (Profile → Long-Lived Access Tokens in Home Assistant).
homeAssistant.setupGuideHint: Copy this prompt and paste it to the agent — it'll deploy Home Assistant, install integrations, and connect your devices as automatically as it can, handing back to you only for account sign-in (e.g. Xiaomi), then give you a URL + token to paste above.
homeAssistant.setupPrompt:
First, check for the bundled helper: run `ha-setup doctor` (or look for `ha_setup.py` under the skills folder). If it exists, use it — it automates every step below; run its commands and just relay any `ACTION_REQUIRED:` prompt to me (a login URL as a clickable chat link). If it is NOT available, do the steps manually as follows.

Help me set up a local Home Assistant, connect my smart-home devices, and hand the result back so I can link it to this agent.

Guiding principle: do as much as you can YOURSELF — via HA's REST API (`/api/…`), its WebSocket API (`/api/websocket`, which drives everything the HA UI can do, including `config_entries/flow` to add and configure integrations), and file operations inside the HA Docker container. Don't make me click through the HA UI step by step. Only hand control back to me for things that genuinely need my credentials or approval (signing into my Xiaomi account, approving an OAuth screen). When you do, give me the login/authorization URL as a clickable link in the chat (not buried in a wall of text) so I can open it, sign in on the official page, and then you take over and finish the flow.

Steps:
1. Detect my OS and whether Docker is installed; if not, guide me through installing it.
2. Deploy Home Assistant (official image `ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:stable`, port 8123). Set internal_url/external_url to the address I'll use (e.g. http://localhost:8123). Give exact commands and run them.
3. Open http://localhost:8123 and finish onboarding (create the admin user). If the browser shows ERR_FAILED on an auth_callback URL, ignore it and reopen http://localhost:8123.
4. Create a Long-Lived Access Token now (profile → Security → Long-Lived Access Tokens) and use it to authenticate all the API calls below. (I'll paste this same token into NarraNexus at the end.)
5. Ask which ecosystem my devices use, then set up the integration — driving it via the API yourself as far as possible:
   - Xiaomi / Mi Home → install the OFFICIAL "Xiaomi Home" integration (`XiaoMi/ha_xiaomi_home`): download it into config/custom_components/ (from INSIDE the container if GitHub is blocked on my host) and restart HA (`docker restart homeassistant`). Then start its config flow via the WebSocket API. When it needs my Xiaomi login / OAuth approval, give me the authorization URL as a clickable link so I can open the official Xiaomi page and sign in, then continue and finish the flow yourself. Avoid "Xiaomi Miot Auto" (its phone-verification callback fails on localhost). If the OAuth redirect uses homeassistant.local, add `127.0.0.1 homeassistant.local` to hosts.
   - A brand cloud (Hue / Nest / Tuya / SmartThings) → start its config flow via the API; hand me only the account sign-in / OAuth step (as a clickable link, same as above).
   - Local Zigbee / Z-Wave / Matter → set up ZHA / Zigbee2MQTT / Matter; no cloud account needed.
   - Not sure / a mix → ask me what devices I have.
6. Verify it yourself: call `/api/states` and confirm my devices show up as entities; tell me how many.
7. Give me back the base URL and the token so I can paste them into the Smart Home panel FOR THIS SAME AGENT.

Ask before assuming anything (OS, ecosystem, account region, devices), confirm each step worked, check the HA logs when something fails, and prefer automating over instructing me.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.hint: What leaves this machine, and your switches for it.
privacy.analyticsDesc: Allow NarraNexus to store product usage metadata for analysis. In cloud mode it is stored in a NarraNexus-managed database; in local or desktop mode it stays on this device. On the cloud web version, anonymous page-interaction data is also sent to Google Tag Manager, a third-party analytics service; turning this off stops it. Conversation content is never collected.
privacy.telemetryDesc: Send this install's service logs to NarraNexus's own collector so crashes and failures can be debugged. At the default level this means structured events, warnings and errors — no message content. Deployments that run the "full" level (managed sandboxes, debug setups) ship whole log lines, which can include message content that services log. Nothing goes to any third party.
privacy.telemetryTiming: Turning it off takes effect within seconds. If telemetry was already off when the app started, turning it on takes effect at the next launch.
privacy.telemetryManaged: Managed by your deployment (environment setting) — the switch is not available here.
privacy.telemetryManagedCloud: Your administrator controls diagnostic telemetry for this install.
privacy.telemetryUnavailable: Telemetry state could not be loaded — the switch is hidden rather than guessed. Reload to retry.
privacy.telemetryError: The change could not be saved. The switch shows the actual current state.
